questions.stem: In the stock market, why does a company pay a dividend to a shareholder?
options: Because the shareholder works for the company
Because regulators require all companies to pay dividends
Because the company is keeping the shareholder's money for a period and investing it in its business to generate revenue, a share of which is returned
Because the share price has fallen
Because the shareholder has sold the stock
questions.explanation: The company holds and invests the user's money for a duration, and a percentage of the resulting revenue is shared back as a dividend.

questions.stem: What do users of mobile applications and social media portals give to those companies in place of money?
questions.explanation: Users give their data, such as buying and selling behaviour, search trends and social interactions, rather than paying money.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT named as an example of the data users hand over to platforms?
questions.explanation: The examples named are buying and selling behaviour, search trends and family and friends interactions; bank account balances are not mentioned.

questions.stem: For what purposes do companies such as Facebook, Amazon and Alibaba use the data collected from end-users?
options: Marketing and advertisement, and selling services to production houses, industries and inventory houses
questions.explanation: The collected data is used for marketing and advertisement and for selling services to production houses, industries, inventory houses and others.

options: A tax paid by companies on stored data
The return a company earns from selling its data warehouse
A discount on cloud storage for large datasets
Giving dividends to end-users in exchange for hosting their data with companies such as Facebook, Twitter or Amazon
The interest paid on a data-centre loan
questions.explanation: Data Dividend means sharing revenue with the end-users whose data the platforms host and monetise.

questions.stem: In the Data Dividend argument, who is the ENTITY described as the core participant in data generation that currently receives nothing?
questions.explanation: End-users generate the data on which the companies make fortunes, yet nothing has been shared with them.

questions.stem: Who is said to need an understanding of Data Dividend?
options: Everyone, whether IT professional or end user
questions.explanation: Data Dividend is described as something everyone must know, whether IT professional or end user.

questions.stem: Which company is NOT named among the examples of platforms that monetise user data?
questions.explanation: The examples named are Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, Amazon and Alibaba; Netflix is not mentioned.

questions.stem: In the stock-market comparison used to explain Data Dividend, how often is a dividend typically paid?
options: Only when the stock is sold
questions.explanation: The company pays the shareholder a certain amount on a quarterly or annual basis.

questions.stem: What outcome is anticipated for the Data Dividend trend?
options: Platforms will stop collecting user data
Users will have to start paying money instead of data
The time is not far when this trend will start benefiting end-users
Regulators will ban revenue sharing with users
Dividends will be paid only to corporate customers
questions.explanation: The expectation is that platforms will begin sharing revenue with end-users, and that this trend is not far off.
